'''Redaction''' is the pluggable tool that scrubs secrets out of messages and
tool output before delivery. Since the extraction, core no longer redacts secrets
itself: a global setting names the MCP tool that performs redaction, and the
default empty value means '''no redaction at all'''.

== Architecture ==

* Core's former <code>src/safety.rs</code> was deleted; there are no
  <code>crate::safety</code> references left.
* A global setting <code>redaction_tool</code> in the general category defines
  which MCP tool performs redaction. The default <code>""</code> passes messages
  and tool output through unchanged.
* The setting is wired into the agent configuration and the writable settings
  keys, so <code>PUT /settings</code> works and the option is surfaced in the UI.
* The invocation point is <code>enqueue_delivery</code>: when the setting is
  empty the content is delivered unchanged; when set, core invokes the configured
  tool with <code>{"text": &lt;content&gt;}</code> and '''fails open''' on error,
  because a redaction error must never break delivery.

|what=pluggable secret redaction via the redaction_tool setting

== The redaction plugin ==

The shipped plugin is a Python MCP plugin exposing the bare tool name
<code>redact</code>; the agent qualifies it as
<code>redaction__redact</code> through the
<code>{plugin}__{tool}</code> convention. It takes the text to redact and an
optional mask, and returns the redacted string. It replicates the exact patterns
formerly hardcoded in core, for behavior parity:

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Pattern class !! Example shape
|-
| API keys || a key that starts with the common provider prefix
|-
| JSON web tokens || a three-part token beginning with <code>eyJ</code>
|-
| Connection strings || <code>postgres://</code> or <code>mysql://</code> URLs
|-
| Cloud access keys || access key ids with the AWS four-letter prefix
|-
| Private keys || a PEM block between its BEGIN and END markers
|-
| Chat tokens || a token with the Slack <code>xox</code> prefix
|-
| Long base64 blobs || long base64-ish strings
|}

Pseudo-matches shorter than 8 characters are skipped. The default mask is
<code>[REDACTED &lt;type&gt;]</code>, and the mask is overridable per call.

A name-prefix pitfall was fixed here: the first version exposed the tool as
<code>redaction_redact</code> (double-prefixed), so the delivery path split it
into server <code>redaction</code> plus tool <code>redact</code>, failed with
<code>Unknown tool: redact</code>, and fell back to delivering the secret
unchanged. Exposing the bare tool name fixed it.

== Test coverage ==

A dedicated deployment test group posts a fake secret to a test channel and
asserts both branches:

# with <code>redaction_tool</code> empty, the delivered reply is unchanged;
# with <code>redaction_tool</code> set, the secret is replaced by the mask.

The test restores the setting afterwards. The group passed first in the dev
stack and then as part of the full suite.

== Relationship to the secrets store ==

Redaction protects content that is '''already in flight'''. The base32 secret and
full enrollment URIs are secrets in their own right and belong only in the
[[Secrets Store]]; a short base32 value or a six-to-eight digit code is not
matched by the default patterns, so the agent itself must not echo them. Never
commit an enrollment URI, a base32 secret or an enrollment JSON to any repo.
